pr_title: feat(worker): Add sourcemap support for worker bundles
pr_body:
<!-- Thank you for contributing! -->

### Description

Improves the [built-in worker plugin](https://github.com/vitejs/vite/blob/d2fc1a1ead1363a15dfcc25fce8587f03289b590/packages/vite/src/node/plugins/worker.ts) to support emitting sourcemaps for generated worker bundles. Closes #5395.

Tests have been added to validate that sourcemaps are generated for inline, non-inline, and shared workers.
<!-- Please insert your description here and provide especially info about the "what" this PR is solving -->

### Additional context

<!-- e.g. is there anything you'd like reviewers to focus on? -->

3 additonal test packages have been added:

-   `sourcemap`
-   `sourcemap-hidden`
-   `sourcemap-inline`

Each of these packages are copied from the `worker` test package and adds a `vite.config.ts` to enable sourcemaps for the respective test case (`true`, `hidden`, and `inline`). The actual test code validates that the `.js.map` files are created and additionally that the source files link to them using a `//# sourceMappingURL=` comment.

One tricky edge case is the scenario where non-inline sourcemaps are being used with inline workers. In this case, the embedded comment has to use the full path (basepath + fileName) instead of simply using the file name. The tests don't address this case, partly because querying the inlined worker code would be pretty messy and it is something where manually running the playground catches the issue pretty easily.

Other details are mentioned via comments in `worker.ts`.

issue_context.title: Sourcemaps for Web Worker bundles
issue_context.body:
### Clear and concise description of the problem

Vite's web worker plugin doesn't appear to support generating sourcemaps.
I ran into this while attempting to migrate [a project](https://github.com/casual-simulation/casualos) from Webpack and noticed that Rollup produced a warning like this:
```
Sourcemap is likely to be incorrect: a plugin (vite:worker) was used to transform files,
but didn't generate a sourcemap for the transformation. Consult the plugin documentation for help
```
Additionally, it was pretty easy to tell that sourcemaps were being created for files imported via an entry chunk (e.g. `index.html`) but not worker imports (e.g. `./myWorker.js?worker`).

Looking at the [worker plugin source](https://github.com/vitejs/vite/blob/61b4b39acd4c122b26a6c91c45bb0727728da7a3/packages/vite/src/node/plugins/worker.ts), it appears that it was never made to support sourcemaps since it only [operates on the bundle code](https://github.com/vitejs/vite/blob/61b4b39acd4c122b26a6c91c45bb0727728da7a3/packages/vite/src/node/plugins/worker.ts#L71).

This is really only an issue for builds (`command === "build"`). Since modules are preserved when serving, no Rollup build is required and so the sourcemaps are generated via the typical means.

### Suggested solution

From what I can tell, the worker plugin [triggers a Rollup build](https://github.com/vitejs/vite/blob/61b4b39acd4c122b26a6c91c45bb0727728da7a3/packages/vite/src/node/plugins/worker.ts#L58) for the imported file, [generates it](https://github.com/vitejs/vite/blob/61b4b39acd4c122b26a6c91c45bb0727728da7a3/packages/vite/src/node/plugins/worker.ts#L67), and then wraps the output code based on whether it is [inline](https://github.com/vitejs/vite/blob/61b4b39acd4c122b26a6c91c45bb0727728da7a3/packages/vite/src/node/plugins/worker.ts#L78) or [not](https://github.com/vitejs/vite/blob/61b4b39acd4c122b26a6c91c45bb0727728da7a3/packages/vite/src/node/plugins/worker.ts#L110). The result is either some code that points to a object URL or an [asset URL](https://github.com/vitejs/vite/blob/61b4b39acd4c122b26a6c91c45bb0727728da7a3/packages/vite/src/node/plugins/worker.ts#L95).

The Rollup build produces sourcemaps based on the config, but those sourcemaps are not emitted. Since at its core the plugin generates a file and then returns a new piece of code that references the file (either as a base64 blob or a URL), I think it should be possible to detect the sourcemap and emit the sourcemap file and/or add the associated comment to the generated bundle.

Funny enough, this solution wouldn't solve the Rollup warning but it would appear to solve the core issue.

I'm more than willing to give a go at implementing this by the way.
